title: crossing-fingerprints-are-verified
intention: A gate crossing produces a cryptographic certificate — a sha256 over the crossing record's canonical JSON — so passage is provable and tamper-evident after the fact without re-running the gate or trusting only the git history.
why: The crossing record in history.json is the record of truth for gate passage (Law 7). Today it is a plain JSON object — editable in place with nothing noticing until the next git diff or build_inspector run. A fingerprint makes the record self-verifying: the hash travels with the record, and a verifier re-hashes to check. Two things git alone does not give: (1) in-place-edit detection before commit, (2) portable verification from the record alone without git history.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the certificate is the receipt that Law 8 was satisfied at a specific crossing.
Law 7 — errors are loud and permanent in records of truth; a fingerprinted crossing record cannot be silently edited.
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics; the fingerprint makes tamper-evidence structural rather than relying on git discipline.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: the tester runs proof teeth — a fingerprinted record verifies, a tampered record does not, a record without a fingerprint is flagged. FEEDS BACK: a red routes to the builder with the tampered field and both hashes.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when every emit() crossing carries a fingerprint field verifiable by re-hashing, and an in-place edit of the record changes the hash. WRONG INTENT if the fingerprint requires re-running the gate (re-derivation, not a certificate), if nothing ever verifies it (ceremony — a hash nobody checks is a hash nobody has), or if it duplicates what git's own content-addressable storage already guarantees without adding portability or in-place-edit detection.
falsifier.horizon: Small code change — a few lines in emit() after the record dict is built, plus a matching verifier and sieve. Bounded build.

how.mechanism: After emit() builds the crossing record dict (transitions.py:1582-1638) and before projector.append_entry writes it, compute sha256 over the record's canonical JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ': '), ensure_ascii=False — the same arguments source_fingerprint uses in validation_store.py). Append the hash as a 'fingerprint' field on the record itself.
how.verification: A verify_crossing_fingerprint() function in transitions.py re-serializes the record (minus the fingerprint field) and re-hashes. A build_inspector sieve runs this over all history.json files at each PROVEME crossing.
how.extends_existing_pattern: source_fingerprint in validation_store (sha256 over proof source files) is the existing pattern — same mechanism (hash for integrity), different subject (proof code vs crossing record). The two could chain: a crossing fingerprint that includes the proof's source_fingerprint links the attestations.
